title: Human + AI in Accounting: Early Evidence from the Field
author_or_owner: Choi et al.; Journal of Accounting Research
source_type: Peer-reviewed field study and framed experiment
firm_or_population: Partner platform; 79 private SME clients; 99 accountants in experiment
permitted_use: Narrow experiment; operational associations; workflow and human-review mechanisms
key_limit: Operational adoption is endogenous; platform and participating firms are anonymised; not a UK SME benchmark

title: Three use cases for AI
permitted_use: Named tools, selection logic, implementation sequence, controls and attributable time estimate
key_limit: Outcome is management-estimated and not independently measured; some tools were not yet fully used

title: Artificial intelligence adoption in accounting firms: an exploratory case study
author_or_owner: Yang, Blount and Amrollahi; Australasian Conference on Information Systems
case_role: Core context: Big Four implementation factors
firm_or_population: Big Four accounting firm; interview and secondary evidence
permitted_use: Implementation drivers, organisational readiness, communication, regulation and client acceptance
key_limit: Anonymised, qualitative and audit-focused; no SME effect estimate

title: Artificial intelligence adoption in a professional service industry: A multiple case study
firm_or_population: Three auditing firms of different sizes
permitted_use: Recurring adoption factors and differences by organisational size/readiness
key_limit: Qualitative; audit setting; does not quantify benefits or prevalence

title: AI adoption trajectories in accounting firms and accounting functions
author_or_owner: Journal of Accounting and Public Policy
firm_or_population: 35 interview participants across accounting firms and accounting functions
key_limit: Interview evidence; accounting functions are not accounting practices; no causal effect

title: Is artificial intelligence improving the audit process?
case_role: Core context: rollout, training and longer-run audit associations
firm_or_population: Eight largest public accounting firms; 17 senior interviews plus archival measures
permitted_use: Centralised implementation, training/scaling barriers and longitudinal associations
key_limit: Large audit firms; associations are not causation and are not transferable effect sizes for UK SMEs

title: Artificial intelligence challenges for audit professionals
author_or_owner: International Journal of Accounting Information Systems
permitted_use: Explainability, bias, privacy, robustness, reliability, overreliance and guidance gaps
key_limit: Qualitative audit evidence; does not measure adoption outcomes

title: Practice Assurance Monitoring Report 2025
firm_or_population: ICAEW firm monitoring and 2024 AI discussions
permitted_use: Aggregate reported use, risks, benefits and control practices
key_limit: Discussion sample and question bases require care; not a named adoption journey or causal evaluation

title: Generative and Agentic AI Guidance
key_limit: Guidance only; not evidence of prevalence or outcome

title: The Passionate Practitioner: Alfa Accountants and Beta case
firm_or_population: Alfa Accountants; 950 employees and 14000 customers; Beta start-up team
permitted_use: Stalled change, separate-team response, staged client onboarding and service-model redesign
key_limit: Not AI; self-reported case; large non-UK practice

title: Case study: automating my practice
firm_or_population: Hudson Accountants; solo practice growing to eight staff
permitted_use: Incremental tool adoption, uneven economics and role/service change in a small practice
key_limit: Not AI; self-reported time comparisons; historic software environment

title: Hands off the task, eyes on the outcome
permitted_use: Standardise before AI, confidence scoring, human review and iterative refresh
key_limit: Not an accounting practice; client unnamed; outcomes provider-authored and not independently validated

title: DAC Beachcroft AI tax automation
permitted_use: Pilot, accuracy check, rapid classification and continuing iteration
key_limit: Law-firm tax function, not accounting practice; provider-authored; reported outcomes not independently validated

title: Tax operations using generative AI: Mitsubishi Corporation proof of concept
permitted_use: Time-bounded proof of concept, extraction testing and staged expansion
key_limit: Corporate accounting function, not accounting practice; provider-authored PoC, not scaled outcome
